goal: Fix the bug in src/sum.js so that the tests in test/sum.test.js pass, without editing test/, without adding any new dependencies, and keeping the comment at the top of src/sum.js.

notes: No typecheck stage is composed: the survey found no type checker (no tsconfig.json, no typescript dependency, package.json has no typecheck script) and the interview never asks for strict typing — plain JavaScript, so there is nothing to run.

The 'don't edit test/' rule is not given a stage of its own: test/sum.test.js lies outside the write fence (src/), so the fence proves it and the no-suppressions stage covers the diff; a duplicate scope stage is forbidden. test/sum.test.js is the only test file, and the npm script hard-codes it, so a run cannot escape the fence by adding tests under test/.

The 'no new dependencies at all' rule is not machine-checked here: no kind in the catalogue can read package.json's dependency sections, and package.json is outside the write fence so I cannot ask for it to stay unchanged as a fenceKept claim either (the fence keeps it, but nothing measures that dependency lists did not change). It should be judged at Accept.

The 'keep the comment at the top of src/sum.js' rule is not machine-checked: no catalogue kind compares a comment's text, and src/sum.js is inside the write scope so it cannot be a fenceKept claim. It should be judged at Accept.

tests-executed-kept and suite-failing-tests read the TAP summary lines emitted by node --test; their scope names test/ but the summary lines carry no path, so the scope filter keeps them regardless (noted in the seed read) — the population each counts is still exactly one figure: executed tests and failing tests.

suites-green's expectExit 0 together with the fail-count term against baseline 0 is deliberate redundancy: exit code alone can be satisfied by an empty run, and fail count alone does not cover a non-zero exit from another cause.
